title: Buzuq Long-Neck Lute
summary: The buzuq is a long-necked lute of the Levant, played with a plectrum on paired metal strings. Its movable frets give the quarter-tone steps of Arab modes, and fast tremolo holds the long notes.
howToPlay: Ten lanes in order of pitch: three on the low string course, six on the higher course, and a tremolo lane for quick repeats.
Notes arrive at the line; strike the matching lane as each one lands.
Begin with the mode run up and down, then try the tremolo line and the lively dance-song line.
A tilde marks a quarter-tone note, between a flat and a natural.
rules: The strings are tuned in fourths from a low G, and the notes follow a Rast-like mode with a neutral third and seventh.
The neutral third is 350 cents and the neutral seventh 1050 cents above the root.
The tremolo lane repeats two quick strokes; each is judged separately.
A stroke on the pulse is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
heritageNote: The buzuq has long been played in Lebanon, Syria and Palestine, and many players know it from folk songs and the music of the twentieth-century Lebanese stage. Its frets are tied on and are often moved to suit the mode being played.
credits: Tradition: buzuq music of the Levant; lines written for this game
